messages:
Eli (New Hire): Hey all, quick onboarding/dry-run question. I'm doing an in-person demo in the conference room tomorrow and when I ran a small load test from our CI I started getting lots of 429s. Which key should I use for an in-person demo (sandbox vs hosted), and is there a fast way to get a temporary demo quota or ephemeral token?

Morgan (DevEx): Congrats on the demo! Prefer sandbox for rehearsals to avoid touching prod quotas. That said, sandbox has tight token/concurrency buckets. For short customer-facing demos we can sometimes provision a temporary hosted burst or an ephemeral demo token tied to your project for a few hours.

Eli (New Hire): The weird thing is sandbox also 429'd. We were on the building wifi (conference room) and testing from a shared CI runner. Could shared egress be the culprit?

Raj (Infra): Very likely. CI runners and building Wi-Fi NAT often share egress IPs which hit proxy-level rate limits. Quick repro: run this curl from your laptop off the corp VPN and from the CI host and compare the response codes:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SANDBOX_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"hello"}' -w "%{http_code}\n" -o /dev/null
```
If laptop returns 200 and CI returns 429, it's an egress/IP bucket.

Eli (New Hire): If it is an IP bucket, what's the fastest fix? I won't have infra time later today.

Morgan (DevEx): Options ranked: 1) Run the demo from your laptop (off VPN) or a cloud VM to get a distinct IP. 2) File a support ticket requesting a short-lived hosted burst + optional temporary egress IP (include project id, start/end, peak QPS, streaming vs non-streaming). 3) Ask DevEx to mint a short-lived demo token for your project (we can do 1-4 hour tokens in urgent cases).

Eli (New Hire): Nice. How do I ask for the DevEx demo token? Any safety/limits?

Morgan (DevEx): DM me the project id and demo window and I'll create a scoped, revocable token tied to the project with strict rate limits. It's logged and expires automatically. We avoid sharing long-lived hosted keys.

Raj (Infra): Also: avoid naive tight retries. If you see 429 from CI, back off and throttle concurrency. Use exponential backoff + full jitter and cap the number of attempts. Our SDKs implement this but custom load generators sometimes don't. See https://console.redwood.ai/docs/retries for recommended settings.

Eli (New Hire): Sounds good. I'll try from my laptop first and DM you the project id, Morgan. If we need infra, who do I tag in the ticket?

Morgan (DevEx): Tag @infra in the support ticket and mention you already asked DevEx for an ephemeral token (helps prioritize). Ticket form: Console > Help > Support > Request quota increase. Include project id, demo start/end times, expected peak QPS and whether you'll use streaming or embeddings.

Eli (New Hire): Filed ticket #11011 per the form (demo tonight 4–5pm, peak ~30 qps, streaming). Also DM'd Morgan the project id.

infra-bot: Support ticket #11011 created by Eli (New Hire) — status: awaiting-review.

devex-bot: DevEx created ephemeral demo token for project redwood-demo-42 30 expires in 3 hours. Token is scoped and logged.

Eli (New Hire): Amazing, that should cover it. Thanks everyone! Will rehearse on my laptop and use the ephemeral token for the in-person run. :thumbsup:
